profile.summary: TranceptEVE predicts the effect of mutations in a protein without training on any experimental measurement of that protein. It combines two kinds of model: Tranception, an autoregressive transformer trained across protein families on unaligned sequences, and family-specific models built from a multiple sequence alignment of the protein in question, namely weighted pseudocounts and a trained EVE model. The input is a wild-type sequence, an alignment of its family and a list of variants; the output is one fitness score per variant. The three parts are combined with weights that follow the depth of the alignment, so a protein with a shallow alignment leans on the transformer.

summary_quotes.text: a hybrid method between family-specific and family-agnostic models that seeks to build on the relative strengths from each approach. Our method gracefully adapts to the depth of the alignment, fully relying on its autoregressive transformer when dealing with shallow alignments and leaning more heavily on the family-specific models for proteins with deeper alignments.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Three sources of evidence are combined at scoring time, not during training. The first is Tranception, an autoregressive transformer with attention heads specialised for contiguous subsequences, which scores a mutated sequence in both directions by default. The second is retrieval from the alignment: weighted pseudocounts at each position, computed with the sequence weighting procedure of Hopf et al. The third is EVE, a family-specific alignment model, whose log probabilities are estimated by sampling and averaged over several trained seeds. The scoring script exposes the combination as two coefficients, alpha for the alignment pseudocounts and beta for EVE, and can rescale the alignment and EVE log probabilities to match the temperature of the transformer.

sections.title: What a run needs
sections.body: TranceptEVE is not a single downloadable model. A run needs a Tranception checkpoint, an alignment of the protein family, redundancy-based sequence weights for that alignment, and one or more trained EVE models for the same family. The alignments and weights for the ProteinGym proteins are published by the ProteinGym project, 5.2 GB of alignments and 200 MB of weights; the EVE models themselves are not in that list of downloads, and the scoring script takes a path to a folder holding them. The reference settings the maintainers used draw 200,000 samples for each EVE log probability and average five EVE seeds, 0 to 4.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The variants are named after the Tranception checkpoint they use: TranceptEVE S, M and L, over Tranception Small, Medium and Large. The published script has all three output paths written out, with Medium left active. A result must name which of the three it used, and also the EVE models, because those are trained per family and are not part of a published checkpoint: different EVE training runs give different numbers. The probability recalibration flags and the alpha and beta coefficients are also part of the setting, and the script runs with recalibration of the EVE probabilities switched on and the coefficients left at their defaults of 0.5.

facts.value: Tranception, an autoregressive transformer with specialised attention heads, plus two alignment-based components: weighted pseudocounts per position and EVE, a deep generative model of the family alignment. The three sets of log probabilities are added with coefficients alpha and beta.

run_guide.summary: Set up the ProteinGym repository, fetch a Tranception checkpoint and the benchmark alignments, then score one DMS assay with TranceptEVE.
prerequisites: A conda environment named proteingym_env, which the scoring script activates.
A Tranception checkpoint: about 400 MB unzipped for Small, 1.4 GB for Medium and 3.1 GB for Large.
Alignments and sequence weights for the proteins to be scored: 5.2 GB and 200 MB for the ProteinGym substitution assays.
Trained EVE models for the same proteins, in a folder given to the script. These are not among the ProteinGym downloads.
Clustal Omega as well, if insertions and deletions are to be scored.
GPU needs are not stated in the sources read.

notes: TranceptEVE has no repository of its own. The code is in the ProteinGym baselines folder and the transformer it wraps is Tranception, so the sources here are those two repositories plus the preprint record. The weights_licence in the structured rows is MIT because that is the licence the Tranception README states for that project, which distributes the checkpoints; the checkpoint archives themselves carry no separate statement, and the EVE component is trained by the user, not distributed, so a row's weights_url covers only the Tranception half of the method. The preprint is not open access at Europe PMC, so only its abstract was read: the weighting scheme that adapts to alignment depth is described here from the abstract and from the alpha and beta arguments of the scoring script, not from the method section. This record may overlap with a separate Tranception record, since TranceptEVE S, M and L are Tranception checkpoints with alignment-based retrieval added.
